notes: Briefing advanced from v0.5.0 (iteration 4) to v0.5.1, which fixes the 'double-click does nothing' root cause (missing '..' in python312._pth + defensive sys.path insert in printdrop_agent.py) plus adds crash.log/MessageBox reporting for unhandled startup errors. backend/agent_dist already shipped only PrintDrop-Setup-0.5.1.exe + sidecar, and the backend test files (test_tscheck_installer_contents.py, test_tscheck_dashboard_download_v051.py) had already been updated for 0.5.1 by the time this session started; I added one new backend test (test_shipped_installer_pth_fix_and_agent_sys_path_insert) to directly assert the '..' line in the extracted python312._pth plus the extracted agent's VERSION/sys.path.insert, since no existing test opened the archive to check that file. Added two new browser checks (owner-devices-download-v051 local + preview) for the updated version label/API. The four GUI-facing criteria (sys.path startup fix, pairing, printers-to-dashboard, crash reporting) have no web DOM to drive with Playwright — they are a Tk desktop window under Xvfb, not the SPA — so they were exercised with the project's own /tmp/e2e051.py script (per seed_facts) under `python -I` + Xvfb, which is the closest reproduction of the embeddable-Python sys.path bug per spec_deviations (no Windows machine available). For the crash-reporting criterion I additionally forced main() to raise (invalid self-test output path) to directly observe crash.log being written with a full traceback; the Windows MessageBox call itself was verified by source inspection only (ctypes.windll.user32.MessageBoxW, guarded by sys.platform=='win32'), as instructed. The one test agent paired during the e2e script ('PC Test 051') was revoked by the script itself and confirmed status='revoked' via a follow-up curl; no seeded/production data was touched. All 6 acceptance_matrix criteria covered by 9 artifacts (several criteria needed both local+preview UI or both API+manual-script coverage). No bugs found; the only non-passing item is the already-known, out-of-scope test_superadmin_scope failure, recorded as an action_item rather than a bug per spec_deviations.
